content.text: The E2E harness itself writes `opencode.json` into every repo, so if lifecycle capture misses the pre-prompt baseline once, that file is guaranteed to be misattributed as agent work. I’m pulling the exact test-harness and code references so the diagnosis is concrete.

The remaining OpenCode failure is a different bug from the `turn-start` race. The shadow branch is surviving because session tracking is picking up OpenCode’s own repo files as agent work.

Evidence:
- The E2E harness always writes `opencode.json` for OpenCode runs in [repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/e2e/testutil/repo.go:116).
- OpenCode also owns `.opencode/`, exposed via `ProtectedDirs()` in [opencode.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/opencode.go:40), but lifecycle tracking does not use protected dirs at all.
- `DetectFileChanges` only filters `.entire/...` via `paths.IsInfrastructurePath` in [state.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/state.go:237), and `FilterAndNormalizePaths` does the same in [state.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/state.go:357).
- Once those files get into `FilesTouched`, carry-forward/cleanup behaves correctly and keeps the shadow branch alive, because it sees remaining uncommitted agent changes in [content_overlap.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/content_overlap.go:383).

That matches the CI artifact: after `src/b.go` was committed, the only remaining carried-forward files were `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` and `opencode.json`, so cleanup never fired.

My read:
- Root cause: lifecycle/state filtering is too narrow.
- Trigger: if pre-prompt baseline is missed or incomplete in an OpenCode run, setup files leak into `FilesTouched`.
- Result: stash/amend/post-exit flows leave an OpenCode shadow branch behind even though user code is fully committed.

Next fix I’d make:
1. Teach lifecycle/state file filtering to exclude agent protected paths, not just `.entire`.
2. Add explicit exclusion for `opencode.json`, since it is a protected repo file but not inside a protected dir.
3. Add a regression test in `state_test.go` around `DetectFileChanges`/`FilterAndNormalizePaths` for `.opencode/...` and `opencode.json`.

If you want, I can patch that next.

That CI run shows the stash fix landed, but there are still 3 OpenCode failures:

- `TestAgentAmendsCommit`
- `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`
- `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`

What changed:
- `TestStashModificationsToTrackedFiles` now passes in this run.
- `TestEndedSessionUserCommitsAfterExit` also passes now.
- So the OpenCode setup-file leak is fixed.

What the remaining failures look like:
- `TestAgentAmendsCommit`: the first agent commit happened before any OpenCode `session-start` or `turn-start` hook was recorded. In the artifact log, `prepare-commit-msg` says `no active sessions`, then only later do we see `turn-end`, which skips checkpointing because it detects no uncommitted files.
- `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`: same shape. Turn 1 is tracked correctly, but Turn 2 commits before a new `turn-start` exists. `prepare-commit-msg` only sees the old idle session with `docs/turn1.md`, finds no overlap with staged `docs/turn2a.md`/`docs/turn2b.md`, and skips linking. Then `turn-end` for the second prompt happens after the commit, too late to condense.
- `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`: different symptom. Here `session-start` and `turn-start` do happen, and `prepare-commit-msg` adds `Entire-Checkpoint: e52dc0ffad73`, but there is no corresponding `post-commit` log or metadata-branch advance afterward. So this one is not the same overlap bug; it looks more like the post-commit path is not firing or not completing for that interactive agent commit.

So the current state is:
- One bug fixed: setup/config files no longer keep shadow branches alive.
- One remaining class still open: OpenCode sometimes commits before the plugin emits the turn/session hook for that prompt.
- Another possibly separate bug: interactive agent commit has trailer injection but no checkpoint condensation afterward.

Useful artifact references:
- Job: `71647442550`
- Run: `24512566028`
- Artifact root: `e2e/artifacts/2026-04-16T13-22-45`

My recommendation is to trace the OpenCode plugin event model next, specifically whether some commit-producing flows bypass the current `turn-start` detection entirely. The strongest target is still [entire_plugin.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts), not the manual-commit strategy.

If you want, I can inspect the plugin logic against these two remaining commit-before-hook cases next.
yes, please do

I’m tracing the OpenCode plugin against these failing flows now. The goal is to see which user-message/commit path skips `turn-start` or `post-commit` and whether the plugin’s event triggers are too narrow.

The plugin’s `turn-start` trigger is narrower than the failing behavior. Right now it only fires on `message.part.updated` for the first `text` part of a user message, which means any prompt path that doesn’t emit that exact sequence will commit before Entire knows a turn exists.

The strongest gap in the plugin is now visible: `turn-start` depends on `message.part.updated`, but the failing `opencode run` cases behave as if that event never arrives before git commands execute. Also, `session-start` is only tied to `session.created`, which looks absent in at least one `opencode run` commit flow.

The plugin is the problem area.

What it does now in [entire_plugin.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts:73):
- `session-start` only fires on `session.created`
- `turn-start` only fires on `message.part.updated` when:
  - the part is `type === "text"`
  - the parent message is already in `messageStore`
  - that message is `role === "user"`

Why that is too narrow:
- In `TestAgentAmendsCommit`, the first commit happens before any `session-start` or `turn-start` log exists. That means `opencode run` reached git hooks without emitting the exact `session.created` / `message.part.updated` sequence the plugin expects.
- In `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`, Turn 1 is tracked, but Turn 2’s commit happens before a new `turn-start`. `prepare-commit-msg` only sees the old idle session, so it skips linking because staged files don’t overlap with Turn 1’s files.
- In `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`, `session-start` and `turn-start` do fire, and `prepare-commit-msg` adds a trailer, but there is no later `turn-end` or `post-commit` log in the artifact. That suggests another missing event path after the agent commit, but it still points back to plugin event coverage rather than strategy logic.

Most likely root cause:
- OpenCode does not reliably emit `message.part.updated` for every prompt path before tool execution.
- Some `opencode run` flows also do not reliably emit `session.created` early enough for us to depend on it.
- The plugin needs fallback triggers based on broader events, not just one specific part-update path.

Concrete fix direction:
1. Treat `message.updated` for a user message as a fallback `turn-start` trigger.
2. Update `currentSessionID` from `msg.sessionID` on `message.updated`, not just from `session.created`.
3. Add a fallback `session-start` when we first observe a session ID on a message/status event and haven’t started that session yet.
4. Add plugin tests for those fallbacks, because current tests only assert:
   - session-start is guarded
   - turn-start is sync
   They do not assert alternate trigger paths.

My recommendation:
- Patch the plugin so `message.updated` can initialize session state and fire `turn-start` if `message.part.updated` never arrives.
- Then add a regression test that requires fallback `turn-start` logic to exist in the generated plugin text.

If you want, I can implement that next.
let's do that
I’m patching the plugin to treat `message.updated` as a fallback source of session and turn starts, then I’ll add string-level plugin tests to lock that behavior in.
or wait: can you confirm your theory from the artifacts?

Yes, with one caveat.

What the artifacts do confirm:
- `TestAgentAmendsCommit`:
  - The first git commit happens before any OpenCode lifecycle start hook is recorded.
  - In the artifact log, `prepare-commit-msg` logs `no active sessions`, then later `turn-end` arrives and says `no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint`.
  - That strongly supports the theory that some `opencode run` commit flows bypass or delay the plugin’s current `session.created` / `message.part.updated` start path.

- `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`:
  - Turn 1 is tracked normally.
  - For Turn 2, the commit happens before a new `turn-start` is recorded.
  - `prepare-commit-msg` sees only the old idle session with `files_touched=["docs/turn1.md"]`, then logs:
    - staged `docs/turn2a.md` / `docs/turn2b.md` not in `files_touched`
    - `session has no new content`
    - `no content to link`
  - Then `turn-end` for the second prompt arrives afterward.
  - That strongly supports the same theory: the plugin missed the start of Turn 2 before the commit.

What the artifacts do not fully confirm:
- `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit` is different.
  - There, `session-start` and `turn-start` both do happen.
  - `prepare-commit-msg` adds `Entire-Checkpoint: e52dc0ffad73`.
  - But the artifact has no later `post-commit` or `turn-end` log for that session, and the metadata branch never advances.
  - So that failure is not explained by the same missing-`turn-start` theory alone.

So the confirmed conclusion is:
- The current plugin start detection is definitely too narrow for some `opencode run` flows.
- That explains `TestAgentAmendsCommit` and `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`.
- It does not fully explain `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`; that one likely needs separate tracing around missing `post-commit` or missing end-of-turn event delivery after the agent commit.

So the theory is confirmed for 2 of the 3 failures, and only partially for the 3rd.
and the changes we did earlier in this branch can't be the reason for any of this?

They are not the cause of the two `opencode run` failures, based on the artifact sequence.

Why:
- The earlier changes on this branch were:
  - `turn-start` switched from async to sync in [entire_plugin.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts:118)
  - state filtering now ignores `.opencode/**` and `opencode.json` in [state.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/state.go:228)
- Those changes only affect:
  - ordering after `turn-start` has already fired
  - file-tracking of OpenCode setup files

For the remaining failures:
- `TestAgentAmendsCommit`: the artifact shows no `session-start` or `turn-start` before the commit. A sync `turn-start` cannot help if `turn-start` never fired at all.
- `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`: same issue on Turn 2. The problem is absence of the new turn-start event before commit, not ordering after it.
- The setup-file filter cannot cause either of those checkpoint-advance failures; it only removes false-positive tracked files and already fixed the stash/shadow-branch issue.

The only one I would not rule out completely is `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`:
- It does get `session-start`, `turn-start`, and trailer injection.
- Then the artifact is missing the expected later `post-commit`/`turn-end` evidence.
- Our branch changes do not obviously target that path, so I do not think they caused it, but the artifact does not let me prove “impossible” yet.

So the clean answer is:
- For `TestAgentAmendsCommit` and `TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn`: no, our earlier branch changes are not the reason.
- For `TestInteractiveAttributionOnAgentCommit`: I see no evidence that our changes caused it, but I can’t exclude indirect interaction without tracing that specific path further.
ok, let's continue fixing
I’m proceeding with the plugin fallback fix now: broaden session/turn-start detection in OpenCode, then add targeted plugin tests that would have caught the two confirmed `opencode run` failures.

I’m making the fallback explicit in the plugin now: `message.updated` will initialize the session when needed and fire a sync `turn-start` for user messages even if `message.part.updated` never arrives. Then I’ll lock that into `hooks_test.go`.

content.text:
Yes. The OpenCode source supports the theory.

Strong confirmations from the source:
- User messages are persisted before their parts.
  - In [prompt.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/opencode/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:1276), OpenCode does:
    - `yield* sessions.updateMessage(info)`
    - then `for (const part of parts) yield* sessions.updatePart(part)`
- Those are separate sync events.
  - `updateMessage()` publishes `message.updated` in [session.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/opencode/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:474)
  - `updatePart()` publishes `message.part.updated` in [session.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/opencode/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:480)
- The event schema also treats them as distinct events.
  - See [message-v2.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/opencode/packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:462)

What that means for our plugin:
- Relying only on `message.part.updated` for `turn-start` was too narrow.
- OpenCode’s own prompt flow creates the user message first, and only later emits part updates.
- So using `message.updated` as a fallback `turn-start` trigger is justified by the source design, not just by CI artifacts.

A second useful confirmation:
- `session.status` idle is emitted independently in [status.ts](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/opencode/packages/opencode/src/session/status.ts:74), so our `turn-end` mapping to `session.status` is still grounded.

One caveat:
- I did not find a source-level proof that `session.created` is always emitted before every `opencode run` commit-producing path in a way our plugin can rely on operationally.
- But given the source above, `message.updated` is clearly a safer start signal than waiting for `message.part.updated`.

So the fallback change is defensible from the OpenCode source itself.
